meta.title: J-Screen — You talk. The TV handles it.
meta.description: J-Screen turns the TV you already own into Jota's screen: it answers without covering what you watch, your phone is the remote, and everything stays on your network.

s1.headline: You talk. The TV handles it.
s1.subhead: The TV you already own, turned into Jota's screen.
s1.caption: Your TV, when nobody's using it.

s2.caption1: You're watching something. Jota answers up top, without pausing anything.
s2.caption2: And what it has pending stays in sight.

s3.caption1: When there's screen to spare, you see everything it does.
s3.caption2: It opens websites, plays music, launches whatever you ask.

s4.caption1: Nothing to install: it's a web page on your phone.
s4.caption2: Trackpad, keyboard, volume and Jota's voice.

s5.caption1: A code on the TV and you're in.
s5.caption2: You, your family and your guests, each with their own place.

hero.headline: You speak, and the living room light goes off.
hero.sub: Jota is a voice agent that installs on a machine of yours and ties together what you already use: Home Assistant, OpenClaw and the model you choose. You don't have to throw away anything you've built.
hero.testedV: jota-gateway v1.21.0, OpenClaw 2026.10.5 and 4 more pieces

talk.said: OK Jota, turn off the living room light
talk.toolSub: Turn off the living room light
talk.answer: Done, the living room light is off.
talk.note: Example. “OK Jota” is a first version we're still training; jota-voice ships with “OK Nabu”.

map.routeLead: The same sentence, from the inside. Everything goes through one door, the gateway: the client never talks to the other pieces directly.
map.borderLead: Every piece installs on a machine of yours. What leaves depends on the providers you choose.
map.hint: Press “Play the journey” or a piece.
map.s1: The client hears the wake word on the device itself. Until then, no audio leaves it. Then it streams your voice to the gateway in chunks while you talk.
map.s2: jota-gateway checks the client's key and picks the agent: the living room speaker can always go to an agent meant for the house.
map.s3: Transcription is live. The final one, “turn off the living room light”, goes back to the client, which confirms it and sends it.
map.s4: OpenClaw thinks and acts: it asks Home Assistant, connected over MCP, to turn off the living room light.
map.s5: jota-speaker generates the voice sentence by sentence. Text and audio arrive over the same connection: “Done, the living room light is off”.
map.reduced: 1 Client · 2 jota-gateway · 3 Transcription · 4 OpenClaw and Home Assistant · 5 Speech. Press a piece to read its step.
map.cTun: Use it away from home through a tunnel
map.oLlm: The cloud model gets the text
map.oTts: ElevenLabs gets the text of the answers
map.oTun: The tunnel or proxy sees the audio go by
map.allLocal: With everything local, “turn off the living room light” never leaves your network.
map.lStt: If ElevenLabs transcribes, it gets your audio. Whoever runs the gateway chooses it, for every client.
map.lLlm: With a cloud model, what you say goes to that provider as text.
map.lTts: If ElevenLabs does the voice, it gets the text of the answers.
map.lTun: If you expose the gateway through a tunnel or proxy, the audio passes through that service.
map.routeFoot: An illustrated journey, at reading pace. Real timings depend on your machine.
map.borderFoot: Each provider has its own terms on what it keeps and for how long.

keep.title: What you already have stays
keep.lead: Jota doesn't replace your pieces: it ties them together behind the gateway.

rows.how: Over MCP. And the other way round: Jota can be Home Assistant's voice assistant, with jota-speaker over Wyoming and the gateway as an OpenAI-compatible agent.

rows.jota: OpenClaw uses it to think and act
rows.how: Local or in the cloud, inside OpenClaw, with memory, agents, tools and scheduled tasks.

rows.jota: Transcription or voice from a provider
rows.how: You choose it in the gateway. Switching doesn't touch the clients.

rows.jota: Each one is a client with its own key
rows.how: If you lose one, you revoke its key and the rest carry on.
Audio goes up as PCM Float32 at 16 kHz and comes down as PCM16 at 24 kHz, over a WebSocket.

where.title: Where you talk to it
where.screenBody: Ask while you watch a show and it answers at the top, without pausing it. Your phone is the remote and the microphone, with no app to install: type the code shown on the TV and you're set.
where.screenNeeds: You need a mini PC or an old laptop connected to the TV over HDMI, and your phone.
where.voiceBody: It listens for the wake word on the device itself and sends no audio until it hears it.
where.iosBody: Experimental and at an early stage.

notyet.title: What it doesn't do yet
items: One conversation per client and agent: you can't open several from the same client.
If the connection drops mid-answer, that answer is lost. The context is kept.
Reminders need an open connection: if your client isn't connected, the reminder is lost.
You can interrupt an answer, but not a reminder Jota sends on its own.
“OK Jota” is a first version; jota-voice ships with “OK Nabu”.
No client for Windows or ESP32 yet, and no guided install.

close.title: Set it up at home
close.body: Start with the gateway and one client. Everything you need is in DIY and the READMEs.
